When water flows into the inlet valve at a higher elevation, it fills the cylinder and pushes the piston upward. This movement creates a vacuum in the cylinder, which causes the check valve to close and prevent further water inflow. The piston then moves back down due to gravity, creating pressure that forces water through the outlet valve and out of the pump.
